text:
Epiglottitis is inflammation of the epiglottis and adjacent supraglottic
structures. It can progress rapidly to life-threatening airway obstruction if not
treated. The condition is commonest in children.
Pathogens in children include H. influenza type B, types A, F, Streptococci and
Staph. aureus The commonest is H. influenza type B.
In adults a wide range of pathogens, including viruses, bacteria, fungi are
involved but H. influenza type B appears to be the most common.
In immunocompromised hosts, epiglottitis may be caused by Pseudomonas
aeruginosa and Candida spp.
Non-infectious causes include, thermal injury, corrosive ingestion, foreign
body ingestion
Rarely may occur as a result of graft-versus-host disease in transplantation.
